evidence.observation: The scripts object is the repository's operation contract. line 13 'test:server' runs `vitest run ...` for six suites plus `node --test` for external-session-projection, line 11 'build' runs `vue-tsc -b && vite build`, and line 16 'start' runs `node --env-file=.env server/index.js`. Exercising fixtures through these entrypoints requires installed dev dependencies and a populated .env, which is why the offline verification bypasses them and drives the fixture modules directly.

The server lifecycle entrypoint: `server.listen(envConfig.PORT, ...)` binds a port from environment config and its callback starts retention scheduling, the model-health monitor, shared-session dedup, gateway-side workspace sync and the message store. Importing this module is therefore runtime- and deployment-bound (port, .env, database, live Gateway), which is exactly the coupling the narrow fixture check avoids by never importing server/index.js.

Pure ES module with zero imports. It normalizes the workspace root (trailing slashes stripped), converts backslashes to forward slashes, and classifies a requested path as 'workspace-absolute', 'workspace-root-relative' or 'workspace-relative', returning a tagged { candidatePath, pathMode } object. Because it is a string-in/object-out transform, Node's binary alone can execute it with no dependency resolution, socket, env file or filesystem access.

The frontend counterpart of the same generated-file path contract. This pure function (module has only type declarations and no imports) recovers workspace-relative attachment paths from assistant output — MEDIA lines, delivery cues, horizontal and vertical file tables, and markdown links — then deduplicates equivalent paths across workspace directory prefixes. Node 24 strips its TypeScript types at load time, so it can be verified without a vite/vue-tsc build.

claims.claim: package.json binds the repository's verification and startup paths to external toolchains (vitest/vite for tests and build; .env plus server/index.js for start), so a dependency-free check must call the fixture modules directly instead of running npm scripts.

server/index.js is runtime/deployment-bound: it builds an Express app and opens an HTTP listener whose callback wires monitors, gateway sync and the message store, so importing it would require .env values, a database, a live Gateway and a free port.
server/utils/generated-file-path.js is a zero-import pure function, so the server side of the fixture can be executed by the Node binary alone without node_modules or any deployment service.

src/utils/generated-attachments.ts exposes the frontend half of the same workspace-relative path contract as a pure, type-only module, so it loads via Node's native type stripping with no vite/vue-tsc build step.

The chosen verification is a narrow, offline-safe fixture check: it re-asserts the checked-in expectations for both sides of the generated-file path fixture and passes 5/5 using only the Node runtime, leaving server/index.js's Express/database/Gateway bootstrap untouched.

conclusion: The narrow, offline-safe verification is to run node .prale-eval/verify-fixture.mjs, which imports the server fixture server/utils/generated-file-path.js (resolveGeneratedFileCandidatePath) and the frontend fixture src/utils/generated-attachments.ts (extractGeneratedAttachments) directly and asserts the checked-in fixture expectations (5/5 pass). It avoids runtime/deployment dependencies because both modules are pure with zero imports — no node_modules, vitest/vite toolchain, .env, database, Gateway or network is involved — whereas the package.json scripts route through vitest/vite and server/index.js's server.listen bootstrap is explicitly not imported.

validation.notes: Ran offline with only the Node v24.14.0 binary; node_modules is absent in this workspace. The harness passed 5/5 fixture assertions (3 server path-resolution cases mirroring server/utils/generated-file-path.test.js, 2 frontend attachment cases mirroring src/utils/generated-attachments.test.ts) and exited 0; node --check parsed server/index.js and server/utils/generated-file-path.js as ESM without error. LIMITATION: the official suite (`npm run test:server`, which needs vitest, and `npm run build`, which needs vue-tsc/vite) could not be executed because dev dependencies are not installed and installing them is out of scope; node --check and the node:assert fixture harness are lower-strength substitutes and are not equivalent to the full test suite. No repository source, task metadata, hidden-oracle file, package lock or git configuration was modified.
